candidates.summary: Covers the requested Percé Rock stop: a boat passes the rock and lands on Île Bonaventure, home to a huge northern gannet colony, with easy-to-moderate trails suited to kids of 7 and 11. candidates.summary: Restored fishing-village buildings with interpretation; short, low-effort, and a good stop for kids. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.summary: A UNESCO fossil site on the Baie des Chaleurs side of the loop, which is new ground for a family that has done the north shore. It has a museum plus a beach walk that children tend to love. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Bioparc de la Gaspésie
candidates.summary: A small zoo of Gaspésie animals with a compact walking loop, well suited to the 7-year-old as a break on a driving day. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Jardins de Métis (Reford Gardens)
candidates.summary: Celebrated gardens near the start of the peninsula that break up the long drive from Montréal. They are an easy stroll. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Short hike in Parc national de la Gaspésie
candidates.summary: An inland alternative to the coast in the Chic-Chocs, using a shorter trail such as the La Chute trail near the visitor centre. This is moderate effort only if the family picks a short trail. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Exploramer sea museum
candidates.summary: A hands-on marine museum with touch tanks, an easy indoor stop if the weather turns. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: South-shore drive along the St. Lawrence to the lower estuary
candidatesAccepted.summary: First leg out of Montréal on Autoroute 20 down the south shore, with a break at Kamouraska. It avoids the north shore they have already done. Driving time is estimated at roughly 4.5–5 hours. Fuel cost is a rough band. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Coastal Route 132 into the Gaspé peninsula's north coast
candidatesAccepted.summary: Scenic coastal drive with frequent pull-offs, such as the Reford Gardens near Grand-Métis and roadside beaches. It is short enough for the seven-year-old. The duration is an estimate and does not include the stops.

candidatesAccepted.title: Northern Gaspé coast drive to the Forillon area
candidatesAccepted.summary: A winding, dramatic stretch of Route 132 through small fishing villages, ending near Forillon National Park, one of the stops they asked for. It has steep grades and is best taken slowly with stops. The duration is an estimate.

candidatesAccepted.title: Short coastal hop to Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short drive to Percé Rock, one of the stops they asked for, with lookouts along the way. It leaves most of the day free. The duration is an estimate.

candidatesAccepted.title: Baie des Chaleurs south coast drive
candidatesAccepted.summary: Closes the loop along the gentler, warmer southern shore, so they see new coast rather than retracing the north. Beaches along the way make good breaks. The duration is an estimate.

candidatesAccepted.title: Matapédia Valley crossing back to the St. Lawrence
candidatesAccepted.summary: An inland river-valley route on Route 132 that completes the loop back to the estuary. From there, the Rivière-du-Loup to Montréal drive repeats the first leg. The duration is an estimate.

candidatesAccepted.title: Camping Forillon: serviced campground sites
candidatesAccepted.summary: Parks Canada campgrounds in Forillon (Des-Rosiers, Petit-Gaspé) have showers, so they fit the 'simple' tolerance and the shower rule, and they put the family inside a park they already want to see. Access needs were not answered, so site accessibility has not been checked; a family of four needs its own tent or an oTENTik.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel in Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: Simple motels in Percé give a bed and a shower within reach of Percé Rock and the Bonaventure Island boats. This is a kind of place, not a named premises. Early July is busy here, and accessibility needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Parc national du Bic camping or ready-to-camp
candidatesAccepted.summary: Bic is on the south shore, a sensible half-day break from Montréal for a seven-year-old, and its serviced campgrounds have showers. Ready-to-camp tents save carrying gear. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel in Carleton-sur-Mer
candidatesAccepted.summary: Carleton-sur-Mer is on the Baie des Chaleurs side, the new-to-them southern half of the loop, and has simple family motels near the beach. This is a kind of place, not a named premises. Accessibility was not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Parc national de la Gaspésie: cabins or camping
candidatesAccepted.summary: Inland near Sainte-Anne-des-Monts, the park's chalets and serviced campgrounds break up the long coastal drive with something different from the sea. Sites with showers keep within their rule. Access needs were not answered.
